title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive in an automated identification system, occurring at the point where a camera reading is converted into an enforcement action. The plate reader produced a match, and the match was treated as sufficient grounds for a felony stop rather than as a lead requiring confirmation. The failure sits between the alert and the officer's response, not in the camera alone.

Catching it would have required a human check against the source record before weapons were drawn, which is the step the vendor itself says should happen. The facts describe a system whose output was acted on directly, and a deployment in which the verification step did not occur or did not occur in time.

What is not established is why the deputy proceeded without verification, and the sheriff's attribution of the error to a tinted plate cover is the department's account rather than an independent finding.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: A York County, South Carolina, man, Steven Melvin, 42, was held at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread his plate and matched his BMW to a stolen vehicle. The sheriff's office said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy's actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be verified before enforcement.
